title: User handbook
subtitle: Exposure and noise evaluation for camera scanning.

pages.title: Why use FilmScan Tuner?
pages.intro: Formerly Camera-41_exp. FilmScan Tuner helps set the digital camera exposure when digitising C-41 colour and black-and-white (B&W) film negatives with a VALOI setup. At a fixed aperture, it compares RAW captures of clear film base plus fog to find a shutter speed that gives a strong signal with room before clipping. Too much exposure can clip a sensor channel. Too little leaves a weak signal, making noise more visible when the scan is brightened. Designed for VALOI hardware with a CS Light light table, but not limited to this equipment; other camera-scanning setups can also be used.
sections: Avoid clipping in the RAW capture

An empty frame containing film base plus fog (FB+F) normally transmits more light than denser image areas of a negative. It is therefore an important exposure reference. If the shutter time is too long, one colour channel may reach its limit. Measurable information is then lost; making the preview darker cannot restore it.
Exposure reads the original Bayer values and compares signal and headroom relative to LibRaw's linearity limit in R, G1, G2 and B. The aim is a strong usable signal with margin, not the brightest image on screen.
What the app does

It compares RAW files at different shutter times, normally chooses an area away from the edges and plots signal and clipping margin. It proposes the longest actually measured time that meets its criteria. A proposal may need further test captures.
What it does not do

FilmScan Tuner can optionally estimate temporal dark noise, dark-noise-limited S/N and noise-limited bits after exposure selection. It does not measure total illuminated S/N or control the camera. The exposure choice concerns the digital capture, not the original analog film exposure.
Quick start

1. Open FilmScan Tuner from Applications.
2. Use Add FB+F RAWs… to load an exposure bracket of the same empty film sample.
3. Enter Light setup and Film base + fog. Tick Same FB+F sample in all RAWs.
4. Press Analyse RAW images and read Results and Exposure comparison.
5. Verify the selected time with a fresh capture.

pages.title: Installation and startup
pages.intro: The standalone macOS app includes Python and LibRaw. The interface is in English.
sections: 1. Open the disk image
Open FilmScan-Tuner-1.1.3-macos.dmg. Drag the Apple Silicon app to Applications on an M-series Mac, or choose the Intel app for an Intel Mac.
2. Open the app
Eject the disk image and open the app from Applications. The apps are ad hoc signed. The disk image has no Apple notarisation.
Verification

The Gold 200 exposure and dark-noise workflow is tested on Apple Silicon and the Intel build through Rosetta. Testing on a physical Intel Mac will be performed later; macOS 13 has not been tested on hardware.
RAW files and diagnostics
Add your own film-base RAWs with Add FB+F RAWs…. Open log shows the local diagnostic log. Quit the app before replacing it.
Check the download
Compare the installer checksum with the accompanying SHA-256 file. On macOS use shasum -a 256 followed by the installer filename. See INSTALL.md for source setup.
Native RAW reader
The standalone app carries the LibRaw reader for its CPU architecture. It reads undemosaiced RAW sensor values. The exposure assessment expects an RGGB mosaic.

pages.title: Capture files and select an area
pages.intro: Use an empty film frame containing base plus fog from the film being scanned. A negative with a scene, text, perforations or a holder edge is not a suitable empty FB+F area.
sections: Keep the setup fixed

Use the same camera, ISO, aperture, light mode and geometry throughout the bracket. Choose the aperture first and change only shutter time. Start a separate comparison if the light, film sample or setup changes. Light setup and Film base + fog document what was measured.
Add and preview RAW files

Add FB+F RAWs… accepts one or more files. Later selections are added to the list; the same path is not duplicated. The file chooser remembers the latest RAW folder across app restarts. Remove selected removes a row from the bracket, not the original file.
Choose a RAW from the file dropdown to preview it. RAW preview is a display image with brightness adjustment; screen brightness does not determine whether the measurement passes.
Automatic area

Automatic area is enabled by default. The central 70 percent of visible width and height is used, leaving a 15 percent border on each side. The same area is measured throughout the bracket. The app does not hunt for a small favourable patch to make an excessive exposure pass.
A per-Bayer-channel screen checks for substantial structure, large illumination differences or insufficient signal. This assists inspection but cannot reliably identify the physical contents of a film frame.
When a warning requires adjustment

When a warning appears, the app shows the affected image and outlines the proposed area in yellow. Drag a new rectangle over clean empty film or edit X, Y, Width and Height in native visible sensor pixels. Use the same area across the bracket.

pages.title: Interpret the results
pages.intro: Successful RAW reading and a passing exposure are different outcomes. FAIL can be a valid measurement from a file that was read successfully.
sections: PASS, REVIEW and FAIL

PASS: every channel retains at least 1/3 EV headroom at the 99.9th percentile, with too few values at/above the linearity limit to trigger FAIL.
REVIEW: no channel triggers FAIL, but at least one retains less than 1/3 EV margin. Do not increase exposure; try a slightly shorter time.
FAIL: at least one channel has 0.01 percent or more of its measured values at/above the limit. First check the sample and measurement area. If they are correct, try a shorter shutter time.
The reference is the RAW linearity limit after black subtraction, not a JPEG histogram. Loss of linearity can matter before hard sensor saturation.
LOW marks a channel whose median lies more than 8 EV below the clipping reference. Some cameras use LibRaw’s white level as the reference.
Plots and table

Exposure comparison opens after analysis and highlights the recommended or provisional time. The signal chart marks the first measured time when each channel reaches the clipping threshold. The headroom chart marks the 1/3 EV minimum for PASS. Results gives the per-file and per-channel measurements. Shutter times are rounded for display only.
A candidate may need more evidence

The proportionality check compares signal per second to its median for each Bayer channel, using at least three distinct passing times spanning one stop or more. A deviation above 5% in any channel triggers a review before using the candidate. In the Gold 200 test, 1/20, 1/15 and 1/10 s passed the clipping criteria. At 1/8 s the green channels triggered REVIEW. The candidate was 1/10 s with a proportionality warning (maximum deviation 5.23%).
Choose a time with margin

Choose a measured time lists passing times in green and other measured times in red. Red times remain selectable for dark-noise evaluation. Verify a passing time with a fresh FB+F capture. If the series is inconsistent, repeat it before choosing a time.

pages.title: Optional dark-noise measurement
pages.intro: Complete the exposure analysis before capturing dark frames at the selected time.
sections: 1. Evaluate exposure first
Analyse the FB+F bracket and review any warnings. Choose the measured time you want to evaluate and click Evaluate dark noise. Add dark RAWs becomes available when both steps are complete.
2. Capture and add dark RAWs

Click Evaluate dark noise. Capture at least two independent dark RAWs; 8-16 are recommended for a steadier estimate. Cap the lens and prevent light leaks. Keep the same camera, ISO, shutter time and aperture, and a similar sensor temperature. Disable long-exposure noise reduction. Use Add dark RAWs… to select several files, then Evaluate noise.
3. Matching and measurement

The app checks the shutter time against the selected FB+F exposure, camera identity including serial number, ISO, aperture and sensor dimensions. Renamed copies and repeated files are rejected. An excessive dark signal is rejected. Temperature and physical darkness must be checked by the user. The same sensor area and separate R, G1, G2 and B channels are used. Changing the exposure selection or analysis settings clears the dark result.
4. Read Dark noise

Noise is the square root of the mean per-pixel sample variance across dark frames. Stable spatial offsets cancel. Signal is the median FB+F signal after subtraction of the mean dark image. S/N = signal / noise; S/N in dB = 20 log10(S/N). Signal bits = log2(S/N). Effective range bits = log2(usable RAW code range / noise). Unresolved zero-noise or nonpositive-signal results are reported without a numeric ratio.
Exposure comparison places RMS noise, film-base signal and the clipping limit on one logarithmic scale for all four channels. Colour fills the span from noise to signal. The gap to the clipping marker shows the remaining headroom on this scale.
5. Scope and example

This is a dark-noise-limited S/N estimate, excluding photon shot noise. Effective range bits describe noise-limited range; they are not ADC ENOB or the camera bit-depth specification. Total illuminated S/N needs repeated illuminated captures. In the Gold 200 test at 1/10 s, two matching darks gave about 58-64 dB S/N, 9.6-10.6 signal bits and 11.1 effective range bits, depending on channel. The report and source hashes are retained in the local log.

pages.title: After the test, logging and help
pages.intro: FilmScan Tuner works independently. No JSON file is transferred from FilmScan Tuner to PRE or NEG, and neither program needs to be open to use it.
sections: Continue in PRE with current captures

Set the digital camera to the chosen time yourself. Capture the current film's empty FB+F frame and two separate dark RAWs with the same camera, ISO, shutter time and aperture. For the dark frames, block light from reaching the sensor and use relevant matching capture conditions.
Load those files directly in PRE tab 7. FB+F and the dark pair can be inspected with a common sensor area and used for noise and S/N measurement. PRE includes its measured result in the film characterisation delivered to NEG. FilmScan Tuner does not export that measurement and need not be installed for PRE to work.
If something looks wrong
Choose a RAW from the file dropdown to preview it. For a failed analysis, read the status message and inspect the local log. Check that the RAW file and its drive are still available.
Log and retained information

Open log opens the local diagnostic log. The standalone app writes ~/Library/Logs/FilmScan Tuner/filmscan_tuner.jsonl. Source runs write logs/filmscan_tuner.jsonl. The app remembers the last RAW folder. It opens with an empty bracket after restart.
Requirements, edition and licences
This handbook covers the Python app in v1.1.3. FilmScan Tuner uses GPL-3.0-or-later. See LICENSE, LICENSE_NOTICE.md and the bundled third-party notices.
